result.question: Why did Zebul send messengers?

readings.answer: To inform Abimelech that Gaal and his brothers were stirring up the city against him
readings.support: to say, “Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem and are stirring up the city against you.

readings.answer: Because he burned with anger at Gaal’s words
readings.support: When Zebul the governor of the city heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, he burned with anger. | So he covertly sent messengers

assessments.reason: Verse 31 explicitly states he sent messengers to tell Abimelech that Gaal and his brothers were stirring up the city, which is a warning about Gaal.
The sequence “he burned with anger. So he covertly sent messengers” supports anger as a motivating reason; while the key focuses on purpose (to warn), this causal motive is textually grounded.
